_comment: Selectors for YouTube's live_chat frame. YouTube can change this DOM at any time — this file is the ONLY place that should need editing when that happens. Ship fixes as a small selectors-pack update instead of a full app rebuild. Values are plain CSS selectors, so comma-separate a few candidate selectors per field to add fallback tolerance for markup variants — querySelector already treats a comma list as 'match any of these', no code changes needed.
author: #author-name, .yt-live-chat-author-chip #author-name, #header-content-inner #author-name, yt-live-chat-author-chip #author-name
avatar: #author-photo img, #author-photo yt-img-shadow img, #img.yt-live-chat-author-chip img, yt-img-shadow#author-photo img, yt-live-chat-author-chip img
_deletedComment: Confirmed against real YouTube markup (Aug 2026): a moderated/deleted message keeps its renderer element and id — YouTube just sets the boolean 'is-deleted' attribute on it and reveals a sibling '#deleted-state' span ('Người xóa tin nhắn: @...') that was already in the DOM, hidden. The original '#message' content is left in place too (recoverable via the mod-only 'Xem tin nhắn bị xóa' link), which is why detection here doesn't try to read replacement text — it only needs the attribute flip. deletedMessageAttr is the primary signal; deletedMessageIndicator is a fallback selector in case the attribute name ever changes. A full 'remove user' ban is a different path — it removes the node(s) entirely — handled in code via MutationObserver removedNodes, no selector needed.
